newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Forties sees active trade, levels steady.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Forties sees active trade, levels steady.

text.p: The North Sea physical market saw around 7.5 million barrels of crude change hands on Wednesday with much of the action concentrated on Forties where around three million barrels were sold, traders said.

Forties traded between dated Brent +30 and +33 cents. Other grades changing hands included one, possibly two, Brents at Feb Brent -24 cents, a Statfjord (Jan 27-29) at dated Brent +20 cents, two January Osebergs and one and a half million barrels of Troll. Talk of an early Feb Beatrice deal could not be immediately confirmed.

Some traders felt the remaining Statfjord cargoes due to load in January could command a higher premium based on refiners covering requirements which may not be met by Ekofisk following the unscheduled maintenance on part of the pipeline.
On Wednesday Ekofisk operators Phillips Petroleum said repair work may take longer than was originally expected. They had expected the line to reopen on Thursday.
"It's not clear what is happening with Ekofisk but people have to cover themselves," one refiner due to load a cargo in the next few days commented.
February IPE Brent gained ground in late trade and at 1938 GMT was up 22 cents at $23.58 a barrel, up 50 cents from the day's low.
The Mediterranean sour market looked firmer after two Urals cargoes on Tuesday fetched differentials some 10 cents higher than last traded levels.
"It's firming up a bit. Urals is the most interesting grade for refiners at the moment," said one Med refiner.
A small cargo loading Jan 25-27 traded on Tuesday on an fob basis equivalent of Dated Brent -85 cents cif Augusta. A 60,000 tonne prompt loader changed hands at Dated Brent -82 cents.
